reviewer: Codex, same author; no independent or human review claimed
scope: All 6,603 translated paragraph blocks in OLP-0001 through OLP-0710; 3,840 unchanged formal/structural blocks classified separately. OLSIZ-001 through OLSIZ-010, OLPL-001 through OLPL-040, OLPL-044 through OLPL-062, OLPL-133 through OLPL-135 and MGR-JV-0118-FRESHNESS-20260920 are applied in their affected targets; the proposed OLSIZ-011 remains retracted after exact-byte inspection. Paragraph analysis normalizes CRLF/LF; exact full-file hashes remain raw-byte hashes.
method: Direct source-to-target reading, quantifier/negation/biconditional checks, mathematical-context checks, and selected reverse paraphrases. Automated structure checks are separate.

unit_reviews.checks: Audience and intermediate prerequisite preserved; rigorous is rendered without adding a mathematical-rule condition; unfinished upstream status, planned additions, contribution link, attribution-license rights, and project link are retained.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: This open-source collaborative textbook treats formal metalogic and formal methods from the intermediate level for readers whose main background is outside mathematics, especially philosophy and computer science; its exposition remains careful.

unit_reviews.checks: Editorial warning, absence of presentation planning, unsuitable raw PDF, build mechanisms, primitive-operator cases, exercises, draft material, course exclusion, sample builds, driver source, and derived-textbook sources are retained. Both URLs and all driver paths are unchanged.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: This file loads every project component without planning its presentation, so this raw PDF should not be used for teaching or study. OpenLogic can generate course-ready texts, omit selected proof cases as exercises, and exclude draft sections; sample builds and driver sources show how.

unit_reviews.checks: Naive set theory, Button attribution, number-system construction, infinity, and their non-requirement for the logical parts are retained. The introduction now unambiguously modifies the fundamentals of naive set theory rather than calling the introduction itself basic.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: This part introduces the fundamentals of naive set theory and, by including Tim Button's Open Set Theory, also covers constructing number systems and infinity; those topics are unnecessary for OLP's logical parts.

unit_reviews.checks: Sets chapter title translated; ordered six imports unchanged.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: Himpunan means sets; this title's technical sense is provisional and established by OLP-0005.

unit_reviews.checks: Collection treated as one object; empty set; both directions of extensionality; order/multiplicity irrelevance; Richard/Ruth proper names; perfect-number example; and at-most-one empty set retained. The definite-description explanation now expresses uniqueness explicitly. Proper divisor is defined descriptively, and the set-builder readings use a property clause rather than a causal clause. Source existential overstatement is followed by OLP-0010 correction and is not silently rewritten.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A and B are equal exactly when every member of A belongs to B and conversely. To prove equality, prove inclusion in each direction.
unit_reviews.notes: Native possessive remains represented through the element token. The unsupported pembagi sejati calque was replaced by the exact condition: a number divides without remainder and is not the number itself. Source prose uses less than 10 while the display uses 0<=x<=10; both remain unchanged, with the same example result.

unit_reviews.checks: Subset vs proper subset, member vs subset distinction, reciprocal inclusion criterion, bounded quantifiers, and all eight subsets of a three-element set preserved.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: The power set of A consists of every subset of A. If A has n members, its power set has 2^n members.

unit_reviews.checks: N includes zero; Z/Q/R definitions and strict/non-strict inclusions retained; nonzero denominator; empty string Lambda; finite strings versus one-way infinite sequences preserved.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: Every finite sequence from alphabet A is a string; the empty string is included for every alphabet. A^omega contains infinite sequences of members of A.

unit_reviews.checks: Union uses inclusive OR; intersection uses AND; disjoint means empty intersection. Indexed union existential versus intersection universal distinction and directional set difference are preserved. The rigorous-proof instruction no longer adds a mathematical-rule condition; existential and indexing clauses no longer use causal wording; set difference now says directly that the retained A-elements are not members of B. Figure captions and every exercise remain translated.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: The union of a family collects objects belonging to at least one member-set; its intersection collects objects belonging to every member-set. A minus B keeps precisely the A members absent from B.
unit_reviews.notes: Automated checks handle nested token braces within prose-only text fields; displayed quantifiers were reviewed semantically rather than discarded. All repairs preserve the source math and glossary-token sequences.

unit_reviews.checks: Order significance, Wiener-Kuratowski definition, left-associated tuples, Cartesian product, counting proof by disjoint rows, induction exercise, and words convention are retained. The counting proof now states unequal first coordinates as an explicit condition rather than saying they cause unequal pairs.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: An ordered pair agrees with another exactly when their first and second coordinates agree respectively. A times B has n times m members if A and B have n and m members.
unit_reviews.notes: Source models the length-zero word by the empty set while the earlier section names the empty string Lambda. Both source conventions remain; no undocumented identification was added. The conditional prose repair leaves every formula unchanged.

unit_reviews.checks: Uniqueness conditional on existence is explicit; unrestricted comprehension is rejected; both branches of the Russell contradiction, the need for existence axioms, and the conditional later-part reference are retained. unit_reviews.reverse_sample: Extensionality yields uniqueness only if the set exists. Assuming R contains precisely sets not containing themselves forces R in R exactly when R not in R.

unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A binary relation on A is any subset of A squared. Relation E may be arbitrary; its being unnatural does not disqualify it.

unit_reviews.checks: All three philosophical objections preserved: alternative pair encodings, nonexistence of the universal membership set, and the predicate versus singular-term distinction. unit_reviews.checks: Every quantified property and all four exercise combinations retained. unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A relation may be both symmetric and anti-symmetric. Irreflexivity forbids every diagonal pair; failure of reflexivity alone does not.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Independent canon revalidation: repaired conditional scope in three relation-property definitions, made the antisymmetry explanation's modal subject explicit, and clarified irreflexive and asymmetric quantification.

unit_reviews.checks: Equivalence requires all three properties. unit_reviews.reverse_sample: Rxy exactly when the equivalence classes of x and y agree. Modulo n on natural numbers gives n classes.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Independent canon revalidation: removed the false corrects-definition sense, adopted verified Javanese division and remainder forms, and replaced a causal such-that clause in the modular characterization.

unit_reviews.checks: Preorder, partial-order, and linear-order hierarchy; connected non-antisymmetric length example; divisibility on natural numbers versus integers; extension order; strict definitions; diagonal addition and removal propositions, proof and exercise; and the extensionality-like property retained. unit_reviews.reverse_sample: Adding the diagonal to a strict order gives a partial order; deleting it from a partial order gives a strict order, with connectedness retained.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Independent canon revalidation: repaired the category-changing divisibility paraphrase with verified Javanese arithmetic wording and removed its causal existential clause.

unit_reviews.checks: Directed graph includes an explicit carrier, so an isolated vertex differentiates diagrams with the same edge relation. unit_reviews.reverse_sample: The graph is the pair of a vertex set and a relation on it. Same edges do not determine the graph if isolated vertices differ.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Independent canon revalidation: restored the equative force of the sentence identifying the sole difference between a bare relation and a graph.

unit_reviews.revision_reason: Independent canon revalidation: repaired the manager-identified causal readings in formal conditions, made ancestor direction explicit, corrected the binary-sequence membership description, and replaced an unstable paraphrase with the locally defined provisional term nyabang winates.

unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A function supplies exactly one output for every input. The square-root selector on natural numbers returns the principal nonnegative root, including zero. The successor example uses x consistently; its value is x+1.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Independent canon revalidation repaired defining-clause and arrow prose while retaining OLFUN-002 and OLFUN-003 as explicit, source-audited critical formal exceptions.

unit_reviews.checks: At least one versus at most one preimage remains distinct, and both manager-identified causal equation clauses now use direct kanthi conditions. Every function induces a surjection onto its range. The general function explanation now says each input has one unique output, while injectivity separately prohibits distinct inputs sharing an output. Constant, identity, successor and parity examples, the bijection definition, and all three figures remain exact. The bijection prose and caption use the already defined one-to-one expression rather than the unstable kanthi tunggal phrase. Locale token keys and flags still select Javanese adjective and noun forms.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A surjection hits each codomain member; an injection never merges distinct inputs; a bijection satisfies both conditions.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Independent canon revalidation repaired both causal preimage conditions, made per-input uniqueness explicit, and stabilized the one-to-one bijection explanation.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared every definition, proof, and conditional branch after the central audit. The extensionality paragraph now says that set extensionality shows the implicit function principle to be sound and states pointwise agreement for every argument. Equation conditions in the graph proposition and proof are noncausal, uniqueness is explicit, and the last paragraph correctly refers to two notions. OLFUN-004 still replaces the source's relation-on-A-times-B wording with a relation between A and B contained in that product. OLFUN-005 still distinguishes domain-only function restriction from the earlier two-coordinate relation restriction. Both departures remain visible critical exceptions with adjacent finding IDs; no formula changed.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A function graph is a relation between its input and output sets, contained in their Cartesian product. Equal functions with common domain and codomain agree at every argument. Restricting a function changes its domain to C while retaining outputs in B; it is not generally the homogeneous relation restriction by C squared.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit repair of vindicate, pointwise-agreement, equation-condition, uniqueness, and plural-reference wording; confirmed source corrections remain critical formal exceptions.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared every inverse definition, both existence arguments, the Choice footnote, exercises, bijection result, and uniqueness proof after the central audit. Both undo metaphors now explicitly say that the second function recovers the first function's input, and equation requirements are marked as conditions rather than causes. The translated left-inverse proposition and proof retain the OLFUN-001 simple correction A nonempty, exactly supporting the chosen fallback a. Its adjacent note states the exact general condition, A nonempty or B empty, and the empty-to-nonempty counterexample. This source departure remains a visible critical exception. All formulas and the right-inverse Choice disclosure remain.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A left inverse recovers an input after the original function is applied; a right inverse is recovered from by the original function. For nonempty A, an injection A to B has a left inverse by mapping values outside its range to a fixed member of A. More generally this works exactly when A is nonempty or B is empty. Surjections have right inverses subject to the stated Choice principle.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit repair of the inverse-cancellation metaphor and equation-condition wording; the confirmed left-inverse source correction remains a critical explicit exception.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared and deliberately reaffirmed every language-bearing choice after the central audit. Composition order first f then g is explicit in the introductory prose, diagram walk-through and caption, definition, and numeric example. The range of f is required to lie inside the domain of g. The injection, surjection, and graph exercises preserve their hypotheses and conclusions, including the relative-product order. Conditional capitalization joins correctly; no target change was required.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: For f then g, the value is g(f(x)), so composing successor with doubling gives twice x plus two.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit choice-level reaffirmation after exact composition-order and carrier comparison; no target wording defect found.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared every language-bearing choice after the central audit. At most one output rather than exactly one, defined and undefined symbols, and the actual domain are retained; the assignment sentence explicitly calls the B-member the result for x while preserving source math-span order. The total-function explanation now quantifies over every input in A, and the reciprocal example quantifies over every real input other than zero rather than using a spatial everywhere phrase. The partial-inverse exercise makes its unique-preimage condition explicit. The relation proposition now expresses the universal functionality condition as an ordinary if-condition; its existence, seriality, and proof witness clauses are noncausal, and the proof states the unique value as siji-sijine. Graph, totality, and seriality conclusions remain exact.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A partial function may have no value at an input. Its domain comprises exactly the inputs where it is defined, and it is total when defined at every input in A. The reciprocal is defined at every real input except zero. A functional relation gives a total function precisely when every ambient input is related to an output.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit repair of the everywhere-else input scope and universal conditional, plus adjacent direction, uniqueness, and witness-condition wording.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared the three language-bearing choices and all structural blocks after the central audit. All thirteen active section imports remain in source order. The first editorial block separately states enumeration, countability, and uncountability, then distinguishes elementary lists or surjections from positive integers from the abstract bijections with natural numbers. The second block preserves Tim Button's attribution, Open Set Theory use, greater abstraction, and the exact bijection-with-Nat-or-an-initial-segment versus list-or-surjective-range contrast. Gedhene Himpunan and the countability family remain explicitly high-uncertainty source-defined wording because no Javanese foundations witness attests their cardinal senses. No target change was required; this wrapper is not yet imported into the three-chapter reader.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: The chapter includes elementary enumerations as lists or surjections from positive integers, and explicitly attributed more abstract alternatives using bijections with natural numbers or an initial segment.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit choice-level reaffirmation with cardinal and countability terminology retained only as high-uncertainty source-defined wording.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared all three language-bearing choices after the central audit. Cantor's 1870s set-theory motivation, making actual infinity palatable, the medieval attribution, treatment of set size, the distinct three-versus-two finite example, and the negative answer for equal infinite sizes are retained. The next paragraph separately states that every finite set is listable, some infinite sets are listable by infinite lists, and some infinite sets are not enumerable. Tanpa wates kang nyata remains explicitly high-uncertainty source-defined historical terminology because no preserved Javanese foundations witness attests actual infinity. No old textbook zero convention is imported and no target change was required.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: Finite sets can be listed; some infinite sets also have infinite lists. Cantor shows some infinite sets cannot be listed.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit choice-level reaffirmation with actual-infinity wording retained only as high-uncertainty source-defined historical terminology.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared all thirty-one language-bearing choices and every structural block after the central audit. The informal definition requires every member at a finite position, the formal definition is a surjection from positive integers for a nonempty set, and enumerable separately includes the empty set. Repetition remains permitted; duplicate removal, the positive-to-natural shift, finite-or-infinite bijection domains, and the injection characterization keep both directions and all empty cases. Repaired the list-property condition, first qualification, duplicate-removal procedure, respectively pairing, domain clause, equality witness, and explicit equivalence between the tokenized enumerable label and bisa didhaptar. The alternating-integer table retains the OLSIZ-001 correction: -3 appears under f(7), as required by both the formula row and the piecewise definition, with an adjacent localized source note. Ceiling remains a disclosed source-defined descriptive term and no computability condition is added.
unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A set is enumerable when it is empty or is the range of a positive-integer enumeration, equivalently a natural-number surjection or a bijection from a finite initial segment or the whole natural numbers. Repetitions are permitted but can be removed. The two displayed parity functions map, in order, to the even and odd positive integers. The formula gives f(7)=-3, and the corrected table shows it.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit repair of the respectively pairing and enumerable-term identity, plus adjacent property, list, proof, and domain constructions; OLSIZ-001 retained as an explicit critical source exception.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared all eight language-bearing choices and every structural block after the central audit. unit_reviews.reverse_sample: The zig-zag order lists every pair of natural numbers once, and f sends each grid label k to the pair in that cell. Treating a triple as a pair whose first coordinate is itself a pair gives an enumeration of natural triples; iteration gives every finite natural power. The exercises separately ask for positive-integer powers and all finite positive-integer sequences.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit repair of an avoidable English-shaped enumeration verb and the proof's causal property clause, with the grid descriptor retained only as high-uncertainty source-defined wording.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared all fifteen language-bearing choices and every structural block after the central audit. The diagonal pairing values, row-to-row observation, corrected inclusive triangular sum, k(k+1)/2 formula, explicit pairing code, injective pairing definition and encode/decode explanation remain aligned. The inverse's displayed values are introduced as direct properties. Rational, binary-string, truth-function, finite-subset and Nat-cubed exercises preserve their scopes. unit_reviews.reverse_sample: The formula assigns each natural pair a unique natural code, so a pairing function is an injection into the natural numbers and its inverse decodes values in its range. A subset of the natural numbers is cofinite exactly when its complement there is finite. Countable unions require the stated choice assumption for an arbitrary family. An enumeration of an encoding range followed by decoding enumerates the original product, with the empty product handled separately.
unit_reviews.revision_reason: Central-audit OLSIZ-002 repair retained; three already recorded source defects were applied in-body, and the inverse property clause was made noncausal.

unit_reviews.checks: Recompared all six language-bearing choices, four arrays and every structural block after the central audit. This yields h(n,m)=2^n(2m+1)-1 and codes every natural pair. The separate prime-power map is injective but need not be surjective, so its inverse is partial.

The resulting sequence belongs to the same space yet differs from each listed sequence at a specified position. For a proposed list of subsets of positive integers, the set of n absent from its nth subset is itself a subset, but differs from every listed subset. Thus neither space can be enumerated.

A partial-function machine may lack output for some inputs; a set-deciding machine returns a Boolean output for each input.
